findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet raises or misbehaves
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes `cursor.offset` (user-controlled, parsed from the cursor string, which allows negative ints) straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment that the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" is false. Where the slice does not assert (e.g. a start of -5 with a positive stop), the result is wrong, so a crafted cursor returns a 500 or inconsistent data. There is no validation that the offset is non-negative.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: The change to `BasePaginator.get_result` uses `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For any prev cursor, a negative offset from a user-supplied cursor (e.g. `value:-5:1`) now reaches `queryset[negative:stop]`, which raises an AssertionError (500) instead of being clamped. Before this PR the same input would have failed on the negative slice too, but the added comments claim this is a deliberate safe feature. This is a behavior change on a path used by every endpoint using BasePaginator subclasses, and the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check further down becomes inconsistent with the clamped start.

findings.title: Privilege gating on negative-offset feature, and potential data exposure to org-level admins
findings.body: The `optimized_pagination` path is enabled for any member with `has_global_access` (not just superusers), and it unlocks negative offsets that the code comment says give "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". The claim that "permissions are checked at the queryset level" is not a real safeguard, since the queryset is only filtered by organization_id. An untested, user-controlled flag that changes slicing semantics on an audit log endpoint is risky. `organization_context.member` can also be None (e.g. for superusers who are not org members), which raises AttributeError, but only after `request.user.is_superuser` is evaluated false.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError when member is None
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally for every request (even without the `optimized_pagination` param). If `member` is None (e.g. a staff or API-token user who is not an org member), this raises AttributeError and breaks the whole endpoint, a regression for the default path. The evaluation should be short-circuited behind `use_optimized`, and `member` should be null-checked.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key breaks on datetime ordering
findings.body: The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, but the new paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`, which is a `datetime` object, so it raises TypeError. The `value_from_cursor` method also returns the raw cursor value rather than converting it to a datetime, unlike `DateTimePaginator`. As a result, the optimized path fails for every request (or produces wrong cursor filtering).

findings.title: Duplicated get_result and unused/misleading design
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result`. The only difference is the negative-offset branch, and the `else` branch is identical to the base logic. This creates a maintenance burden and divergence risk. The docstring claims performance optimizations that do not exist, since it performs the same queries.

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming uses unadjusted offset
findings.body: `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw `cursor.offset`, which can be negative in the advanced branch, while the actual slice start differs. The condition will not match the number of rows fetched, so the extra row is not dropped and pages can contain an extra or duplicate item.

findings.title: No tests for new paginator or endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator, a new query parameter, and negative-offset behavior with no tests. The PR description is just "Test 1", with no explanation of the feature. There is also trailing whitespace on lines 71 and 89.
